thread:
michael: escalating - ACME PROD reported 429 mid-stream and doubled charges; attaching logs.

priya: got it. can you paste request-id + session-id?

michael: request-id: r-0a1b2c3d, session_id: sess-acme-9f4, customer says client did an immediate reconnect with rotated token. logs:

michael: server logs:
[2026-02-25T15:12:03Z] r-0a1b2c3d sess=sess-acme-9f4 uid=acme-prod INFO stream-start seq=1
[2026-02-25T15:12:28Z] r-0a1b2c3d sess=sess-acme-9f4 uid=acme-prod WARN RateLimitExceeded mid-stream seq=12 tokens=341
[2026-02-25T15:12:29Z] r-0a1b2c3d sess=sess-acme-9f4 uid=acme-prod INFO client-reconnect token=k2 new-conn-id=c-232
[2026-02-25T15:12:29Z] r-0a1b2c3d sess=sess-acme-9f4 uid=acme-prod INFO resume-accepted accounting=NEW_LEDGER_ENTRY tokens=0
[2026-02-25T15:12:31Z] r-0a1b2c3d sess=sess-acme-9f4 uid=acme-prod INFO stream-continued seq=13 tokens=120 billed
[2026-02-25T15:12:35Z] r-0a1b2c3d sess=sess-acme-9f4 uid=acme-prod INFO ledger: +461 tokens total

priya: interesting — resume-accepted shows accounting created a new ledger entry instead of attributing to existing one.

jamie: probable root cause: resume flow keyed billing to auth token + conn id; when token rotated at reconnect we created a new billing record. we should be binding ledger to session-id not token. can reproduce with this client script:

```bash
# repro (stream then rotate token quickly)
TOKEN1=eyJhbGci...k1
TOKEN2=eyJhbGci...k2
SESSION=sess-acme-9f4
# open stream
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN1" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?session=$SESSION&stream_mode=prompt" -d '{"prompt":"long..."}' &
sleep 25
# simulate mid-stream 429 and immediate reconnect with rotated token
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN2" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?session=$SESSION&resume=true" &
```

michael: customer ran similar and saw two ledger rows. they want explanation and a credit for double-billing.

jamie: short-term mitigation: enforce resume auth KID match or require `x-resume-signature` tied to original token. Longer-term: change accounting to lookup by session namespace (session id) and merge resume events to same ledger entry.

ops-oncall: rolling a canary patch now — refuse resumes when the presented token's kid != original_kid. will push to prod-2 region in 15m. monitor logs for `resume-rejected-kid-mismatch`.

support-bot: Ticket #CS-8921 updated: customer notified of mitigation; offering 100% credit for duplicated tokens while we remediate :white_check_mark:

priya: send the customer the repro steps + ask for client SDK version (they're on 2.1.4?). also check if they used connection pooling/proxy.

michael: confirmed sdk=2.1.4, using load-balancer that rotated auth via sidecar.

jamie: noted. I'll open a bug and link to this thread. assigned to eng-runtime. ETA for session-based ledger change: 3-4 sprints. quick canary should reduce incidents.

michael: will offer immediate refund and follow up. thanks all :heart:
